newsitem.title: UK: BG sees profits up after accounting change.
newsitem.headline: BG sees profits up after accounting change.

text.p: BG Plc said on Wednesday a planned change in accounting principles will lead to a rise of 250 million stg per year in annual operating profits.

Finance director Philip Hampton repeated BG's dividend will still be considerably lower than before the British Gas demerger in February, but he added the pay-out cut may now turn out to be less drastic than previously anticipated.
The dividend policy will be revised by September, Hampton said in an interview with Reuters.
"At the time of the demerger we said we would expect the dividend to be reduced materially. This (reduction) might now be somewhat less," he said.
The change in accounting principles is the result of a new pricing regime for BG's gas transportation business TransCo.
BG said it will stop reporting results on a full CCA basis, which will result in a lower depreciation charge and therefore lead to higher profits.
Hampton said the new TransCo pricing regime, announced earlier today, will likely be implemented in October or November.
Under the new regime, TransCo will trim its charges to gas suppliers by a one-off 21 percent in the first year, and by inflation minus two percent thereafter.
The new price controls come after a probe by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission after BG last year rejected proposals put forward by regulator Ofgas.
Ofgas has now followed the recommendations by the MMC, which adopted a regulatory asset base for 11.6 billion stg for TransCo.
This compares with a true replacement cost of 17 billion stg, BG said.
As a result, BG plans to write down the value of TransCo's assets by some five billion stg.
In a separate interview, Ofgas chief Clare Spottiswoode said she was pleased with the MMC recommendations as "they upheld all the basic principles" of her previous proposals.

BG and Ofgas will now be working to separate the gas transportation business from the gas storage operations. The storage activities will be incorporated in a new company which won't be regulated, she said.
